principles: Receipt-backed authority is a cryptographic classification, not a prose claim or HTTP transport flag.
Local/off Koala development must remain free and usable without a Python authority server.
Every production authority claim must bind run identity, provider metadata, command/transcript/diff hashes, envelope signature, and verified AuthorityReceipt.
Parallel planning artifacts are scheduling memory only; they must not become DONE or production authority evidence.
drivers: Prevent process/fact forgery without making ordinary local usage depend on a paid server.
Keep CI deterministic by using in-process fake authority receipts and explicit live-test skip semantics.
Let Claude Code CLI implement under a strict scope contract while Codex verifies independently.

options.name: deterministic-fake-authority-plus-optional-live
pros: CI can verify signed receipt promotion and adversarial failures without network or paid server
Local/off and shadow workflows remain unchanged
Live Python authority integration can be documented and tested only when env vars exist
cons: Does not prove a currently running external Python deployment unless env vars are configured
Still requires future runner/Mac adoption for real production operation

options.name: real-python-authority-required
pros: Closest to production behavior when server credentials exist
Exercises the actual external authority stack
cons: Breaks local/free development and CI when the paid server is unavailable
Harder to isolate CLI classification bugs from external server outages

options.name: status-doc-only
cons: Does not materially reduce fact forgery because receipt-backed promotion remains untested
Leaves M7-M8 dependent on prose rather than mechanical proof

rationale: Choose deterministic fake-authority receipt verification for hard local proof, plus a gated live smoke for external deployments. This preserves free local Koala usage while making receipt-backed L2+ impossible to claim without cryptographic receipt verification.

preMortem.scenario: HTTP accepted:true is mistaken for authority receipt verification
preMortem.trigger: A handler reads accepted:true and sets receiptVerified=true without signature verification
preMortem.consequence: Thin-client evidence could be misreported as production authority
preMortem.mitigation: Keep classifyCliAuthoritySubmission receiptVerified=false and add adversarial tests for transport accepted without verified receipt

preMortem.scenario: Fake receipt does not bind the evidence envelope it supposedly acknowledges
preMortem.trigger: Receipt signature verifies but subjectId/subjectDigest do not match the envelope
preMortem.consequence: A valid receipt for another artifact could promote the wrong evidence
preMortem.mitigation: Classify receipt-backed only after receipt signature and subject binding checks pass

preMortem.scenario: The local matrix accidentally requires a live paid server
preMortem.consequence: Local users cannot run tests or develop for free
preMortem.mitigation: Use in-process fake server/receipt harness and make live Python smoke self-skip unless env vars exist

preMortem.scenario: Parallel Wave report is treated as DONE evidence
preMortem.trigger: Report contains evidenceRefs and dispatch guidance that a gate treats as authoritative
preMortem.consequence: Planning artifacts could bypass real validation evidence
preMortem.mitigation: Assert report authority.productionDone=false and no verified receipt refs; docs say planning artifacts cannot satisfy DONE
